name: Grevillea 'Robyn Gordon'
description: A popular Australian hybrid grevillea (Grevillea banksii × G. bipinnatifida) with fern-like leaves and large red flower spikes for most of the year. Honeyeaters visit it constantly.

toxic.note: The leaves and flowers can cause an itchy rash on contact. Please wear gloves and long sleeves when pruning.

name: Grevillea 'Superb'
description: An Australian hybrid grevillea with large apricot-pink flower spikes for most of the year, very attractive to honeyeaters.

toxic.note: The foliage can irritate sensitive skin. Please wear gloves when pruning.

name: Grevillea 'Honey Gem'
description: A tall Australian hybrid grevillea with golden-orange flower spikes full of nectar. In warm climates it flowers for most of the year.

name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia
description: A hardy shrub with needle-like leaves and red spider flowers through winter and spring. Its prickly foliage gives small birds safe shelter.

name: Grevillea banksii
description: A Queensland shrub or small tree with large red or cream brush flowers for much of the year.

toxic.note: The foliage and flowers can cause an itchy rash on contact.

name: Grevillea robusta
description: A tall, fast-growing tree with fern-like leaves and bright orange flowers in spring that drip with nectar for birds and bees.

toxic.note: The flowers and seeds contain cyanogenic compounds, and the sap can irritate skin.

care_note: Grows into a large tree. Outside its natural range it can self-seed into bushland.

name: Melaleuca viminalis
description: A small tree with weeping branches and bright red brush flowers in spring, loved by honeyeaters, lorikeets and bees. Many compact cultivars are sold under the older name Callistemon viminalis.
pruning: Prune just behind the spent flowers to keep the plant dense and encourage a second flush.

name: Melaleuca citrina
description: A hardy shrub with stiff, lemon-scented leaves and crimson brush flowers in spring, often again in autumn.
pruning: Prune just behind the spent flowers.

name: Melaleuca linariifolia
description: A paperbark tree that is smothered in fluffy white flowers in late spring and early summer, when it hums with bees.

name: Melaleuca quinquenervia
description: A large paperbark of coastal swamps with creamy bottlebrush flowers from late summer into winter, an important winter nectar source for birds, flying-foxes and honey bees.
care_note: Grows into a large tree. Please keep it well away from buildings and pipes.

name: Leptospermum petersonii
description: A graceful shrub or small tree with lemon-scented leaves and masses of small white flowers in early summer that attract native bees, flies and beetles.
edible: leaves, used as a lemon-flavoured tea
pruning: Prune lightly after flowering to keep it bushy.

name: Leptospermum polygalifolium
description: A variable shrub with small white flowers in spring and early summer. It is one of the tea trees behind Australian medicinal honey.

name: Westringia fruticosa
description: A tough coastal shrub with grey-green leaves and small white flowers for most of the year. It makes a good hedge and stands up to salty wind.

name: Correa reflexa
description: A small shrub with bell-shaped red-and-green or pink flowers through autumn and winter, a valuable winter nectar source for eastern spinebills.
care_note: Needs good drainage and some shade from hot afternoon sun.

name: Banksia integrifolia
description: A coastal tree with leathery leaves, silver beneath, and pale yellow flower spikes from late summer into winter that feed honeyeaters, lorikeets and possums.

name: Banksia spinulosa
description: A shrub with narrow leaves and golden flower spikes with dark hooked styles through autumn and winter.

name: Banksia ericifolia
description: A shrub with fine heath-like leaves and tall orange flower spikes from autumn to winter.

name: Hakea laurina
description: A Western Australian shrub or small tree with round red pincushion flowers studded with cream styles in autumn and winter.
care_note: Dislikes humid summers and heavy, wet soils.

name: Buckinghamia celsissima
description: A rainforest tree from north Queensland with long cream flower spikes in summer, busy with bees and honeyeaters.

name: Macadamia integrifolia
description: The macadamia nut tree, a Queensland rainforest native with long cream flower spikes in late winter and spring. Stingless bees are used to pollinate macadamia orchards.

toxic.note: Macadamia nuts are poisonous to dogs.

name: Alyogyne huegelii
description: A fast-growing shrub with large lilac flowers like a hibiscus from spring into summer.

name: Eremophila maculata
description: An inland shrub with spotted tubular flowers in red, pink or yellow through winter and spring.

name: Philotheca myoporoides
description: A rounded shrub with aromatic leaves and white star-shaped flowers from pink buds in late winter and spring.

name: Goodenia ovata
description: A fast-growing shrub with bright yellow flowers through spring and summer that native bees visit.

name: Melastoma malabathricum
description: A tropical shrub with large pink-purple flowers through summer. The flowers are buzz-pollinated by blue-banded and carpenter bees, and the pulp of the berries stains the tongue blue.

name: Hymenosporum flavum
description: A slender tree with fragrant cream flowers that turn yellow, in spring.

name: Elaeocarpus reticulatus
description: A small tree with fringed white or pink bell flowers in late spring, followed by bright blue berries that birds eat.

name: Austromyrtus dulcis
description: A low, spreading shrub with small white flowers in spring, followed by sweet, speckled white berries.

name: Syzygium australe
description: A dense lilly pilly with glossy leaves, white flowers in summer and edible red to pink fruit. It is widely used for hedges.
care_note: Fairly resistant to lilly pilly psyllid.

name: Syzygium luehmannii
description: A lilly pilly with small glossy leaves, pink new growth and clusters of edible red berries with a clove-like flavour in summer.

name: Backhousia citriodora
description: A small tree with strongly lemon-scented leaves, used as a flavouring and tea, and clusters of white flowers in summer.
edible: leaves, as a flavouring and tea
care_note: Myrtle rust can damage new growth in humid weather.

name: Dodonaea viscosa
description: A hardy shrub grown for its papery seed capsules, which turn red or purple in spring. It is wind-pollinated, so it offers bees little.

name: Pultenaea villosa
description: A soft, weeping shrub covered in small yellow and red pea flowers in spring.

name: Acacia fimbriata
description: A fast-growing wattle with fine, weeping foliage and lemon-yellow balls of flowers in late winter and spring. Like all wattles, its flowers offer pollen but no nectar.

name: Acacia podalyriifolia
description: A wattle with silvery, rounded leaves and masses of golden flower balls in winter.
care_note: It self-seeds and is considered a weed outside its natural range, for example in Victoria and Western Australia.

name: Corymbia ficifolia
description: A small, spreading gum from south-west Western Australia with spectacular red, orange or pink flowers in summer.
care_note: In humid eastern gardens it is often grafted onto a hardier rootstock.

name: Corymbia citriodora
description: A very tall, smooth-barked gum with lemon-scented leaves and cream flowers in winter.
care_note: Grows very tall. Please plant it only in a large yard, well away from buildings.

name: Eucalyptus tereticornis
description: A tall gum with smooth, patchy bark and cream flowers from winter to spring. It is a favourite food tree of koalas.

name: Eucalyptus melliodora
description: A spreading gum famous among beekeepers for its pale, mild honey. Its cream flowers appear from spring into summer.

name: Angophora costata
description: A tree with smooth pink-orange bark that sheds in spring, twisted limbs and white flowers in early summer.

name: Brachychiton acerifolius
description: A tree that drops its leaves and covers itself in scarlet bell flowers in late spring and early summer.
care_note: The seed pods are lined with irritating hairs. Please wear gloves when handling them.

name: Tristaniopsis laurina
description: A dense, shady tree from creek banks with small yellow flowers in summer.

name: Waterhousea floribunda
description: A shady rainforest tree with weeping foliage, white flowers in late spring and green fruit.

name: Allocasuarina littoralis
description: A small she-oak with fine, drooping branchlets. Glossy black-cockatoos feed on the seeds in its cones. It is wind-pollinated, so it offers bees little.

name: Citrus australasica
description: A thorny rainforest shrub whose finger-shaped fruit is filled with citrus 'caviar'.
care_note: Thorny. Please plant it away from paths.

name: Archontophoenix cunninghamiana
description: A tall, slender native palm with lilac flowers and red fruit that birds eat.
care_note: Fallen fronds and fruit are heavy and messy. Please give it space away from paths and roofs.

name: Cordyline petiolaris
description: A rainforest plant with broad, palm-like leaves, lilac flowers in late spring and red berries that birds eat.
